# mimux — the self-hosted inbox your agents can act on

> A fast, keyboard-driven email client you run yourself — one Go binary, one
> SQLite file, no third party in the middle. The client is free and AGPL-3.0
> forever; a paid automation layer (REST API, MCP server, webhooks) is on the
> roadmap, so agents can act on an inbox that lives on your own hardware.

Canonical site: <https://mimux.dev/>. This document mirrors the full content of
the landing page for language-model consumption.

## What it is

mimux is a fast, keyboard-driven email client you run yourself. Point it at the
mailboxes you already have, and read, search, triage and send from one unified
inbox — in the browser or as an installed PWA on your phone. Your mail, your
credentials, your machine.

- Source: <https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux>
- Docs: <https://docs.mimux.dev>
- Account and licences: <https://account.mimux.dev>

## How you get it

One command to boot, zero configuration to run:

```sh
docker compose up
# then open http://localhost:8083
```

1. **Start it.** One container, one volume, one port.
2. **Open it.** The first visit walks you through creating your admin account.
3. **Point it at your mail.** Add accounts under Settings → Accounts — OAuth2
   for Gmail and Zoho, app passwords everywhere else. Changes take effect
   without a restart.

One Go binary serves the UI (htmx + Alpine.js + Tailwind) and talks IMAP and
SMTP; one SQLite file holds everything — accounts, credentials, message cache,
sessions, filters, saved searches, OAuth tokens. Back up the directory and
you have backed up everything.

## What it does (all free, all shipping)

- **Unified inbox** across every configured account, plus a per-account view.
  Conversation threading, unread counts and the full folder tree per account.
- **Background sync** — IMAP IDLE with polling fallback, one connection per
  account. Gmail and Zoho over OAuth2, everything else over passwords.
- **Search, streamed** — instant local full-text search, plus on-demand deep
  IMAP server search returned over SSE as results arrive.
- **Compose** — reply, reply-all and forward over SMTP in plain text, rich text
  or Markdown, with local draft autosave, undo-send and scheduled send.
- **Filters and rules** — conditions → actions (move, label, forward, mark
  read, star, delete, notify), running on incoming mail on your server.
- **Keyboard-first** — a full shortcut set: `j`/`k` to move, `e` archive,
  `s` star, `R`/`A`/`F` reply/reply-all/forward, `/` search, `?` help.
- **PWA and push** — installable as an app with an offline fallback to the
  last-synced inbox. Web Push from your own server (end-to-end encrypted
  payloads) or a POST to any ntfy topic.
- **AI, bring-your-own-key** — optional AI compose/reply and translate
  (OpenRouter, Google Translate). Off by default; keys stay in your database.
- **Backup = cp** — all state is one SQLite file.

## Why self-hosted

- **No account to create.** mimux talks IMAP/SMTP directly to providers you
  already use, with credentials that live in your SQLite file.
- **No telemetry.** The application phones home to no one: no CDNs, no
  analytics, no tracking — everything is bundled in the binary. Remote images
  in emails stay blocked until you allow them.
- **Open, all the way down.** AGPL-3.0. One Go binary over SQLite — small
  enough to read end to end, boring enough to run for years.
- **Yours on bad days.** If the author vanishes, the binary you run keeps
  working and the source is yours.

## What is coming (roadmap — not released)

Agent frameworks can search the web and run code, but they cannot read your
mail unless you hand your inbox to a SaaS intermediary. The mimux pro layer
closes that gap on your own hardware:

- **REST API** — messages, folders, search, send, drafts and filters over HTTP,
  with an OpenAPI spec served from the binary.
- **MCP server** — your inbox as a first-class tool for agents: read, search,
  triage and draft from any MCP-capable client.
- **Webhooks** — new mail and rule matches pushed to your automation: n8n,
  Home Assistant, your own scripts.

The line does not move: **a human driving mimux is free; a machine driving
mimux is paid.** The paid layer is automation only, published in advance so its
arrival is a plan being executed, not a surprise.

## Pricing

| | Client | Automation layer |
|---|---|---|
| Price | €0, forever | €49/yr or €99 perpetual — when it ships |
| Licence | AGPL-3.0 | Elastic Licence 2.0 |
| Includes | sync, search, compose, filters, calendar, PWA, push, AI compose/translate (BYO key) | REST API, MCP server, webhooks |

The split is enforced by the build, not by trust: every file in `pro/` carries
a `//go:build pro` tag, `make verify-free` proves the free binary links none of
it, and [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux/blob/main/LICENSING.md)
explains the whole arrangement.

## This page

Self-hosted, cookieless analytics (Umami) run on the author's own server: no
cookies, no third parties, no personal data — so no cookie banner. The page
makes exactly one external request (the analytics script) and renders fully
with JavaScript disabled.
